papers.abstract: Cancer genomes harbor extensive somatic genetic and epigenetic variation, yet large portions of the genome remain inaccessible to conventional reference-based analyses. Here, we demonstrate that pairing a near-telomere-to-telomere (near-T2T) diploid assembly of a donor with deep short- and long-read sequencing of their melanoma reveals that 16% of somatic variants localize to sequences absent from GRCh38, with satellite repeats acting as hotspots for UV-associated mutagenesis. Centromere kinetochore binding domains emerge as focal sites of chromosome arm aneuploidy breakpoints and somatic genetic variation, features we further demonstrate are also present in non-cancerous tissues. By contrast, extensive epigenetic remodeling of kinetochore binding domains appears specific to oncogenesis. Single-molecule telomere analyses reconstruct the cycle of telomere erosion and telomerase-mediated extension during tumor evolution, while haplotype-resolved chromatin maps reveal widespread somatic epimutations impacting regulatory elements. Together, these findings define previously inaccessible dimensions of somatic variation and establish a framework for telomere-to-telomere studies of human mosaicism.

papers.abstract: Rhizobial nitrogen fixation in legume nodules requires precise spatial and temporal coordination between host and bacterial gene expression. Here, we applied spatial enhanced resolution omics sequencing (Stereo-seq) to profile Medicago nodules across five developmental stages, generating a co-transcriptomic atlas of nodule development. Using a mixed-probe capture strategy, we simultaneously detected host and rhizobial transcripts within the same tissue sections, enabling analysis of host-microbe transcriptional coordination during symbiosis. We identified dynamic changes in host cell composition and developmental trajectories and uncovered two transcription factors, MtERF82 and MtDOF53, required for maintenance of the indeterminate nodule meristem. Rhizobial and host genes exhibited stage- and zone-specific expression patterns along the nodule apex-to-base axis. Notably, reactive oxygen species (ROS)-associated stress responses in both host cells and rhizobia were linked to symbiotic nitrogen fixation. Functional analyses further showed that MtERF71 and MtCBF1 promote nitrogen fixation by regulating ROS homeostasis and activating key symbiotic genes, highlighting stress signaling as an integral component of mutualistic symbiosis.

papers.abstract: Recent studies have established that the nervous system is not merely a bystander in tumour progression but can actively remodel the tumour microenvironment through the neuro-tumour axis, thereby promoting tumour invasion, metastasis and survival. Semaphorin 3C (SEMA3C) has been reported to regulate tumour migration, angiogenesis and immune suppression, highlighting its potential role in tumour progression. Although the neuro-tumour axis has been identified in multiple cancer types, its role and underlying mechanisms in gastric cancer peritoneal metastasis (GCPM) remain unclear. We performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) of GCPM tissues to profile tumour cell heterogeneity and identify tumour cell populations associated with neural-related signalling. Candidate tumour-microenvironmental interactions were further investigated using patient-derived organoids and co-culture models, and the identified signalling axis was validated using corresponding in vivo models. SnRNA-seq identified a distinct subpopulation of poorly differentiated tumour cells with pronounced stem-like properties and high SEMA3C expression. This subpopulation was associated with neural-related features and interacted with tumour-associated endothelial cells, thereby contributing to remodelling of the metastatic microenvironment. Furthermore, these cells enhanced tumour-endothelial communication by activating the fibroblast growth factor receptor-associated signalling pathway. The transcription factor early B-cell factor 2 (EBF2) regulates the expression of FGF7 within this subpopulation, thereby strengthening FGF7-FGFR2 signalling and promoting tumour progression. Functional validation further demonstrated that SEMA3C depletion impaired organoid growth and tumour-endothelial interactions, whereas disruption of the SEMA3C-EBF2-FGF7-FGFR2 signalling axis attenuated tumour growth and peritoneal tumour burden in vivo. Additional experimental validation supported the potential involvement of neural-related signalling in the SEMA3C-associated tumour cell state. Our findings identify a SEMA3C+ tumour cell subpopulation associated with neural-related signalling and suggest that SEMA3C promotes tumour-endothelial interactions through the EBF2-FGF7-FGFR2 signalling axis, providing a potential mechanistic link between neural regulation and microenvironmental remodelling in peritoneal metastasis of gastric cancer.

papers.abstract: Recent whole-brain cell atlases have uncovered a consistent cytoarchitectural feature: the greatest diversity of discrete neuronal cell types resides not in the regions with the most neurons (e.g., the cortex and cerebellum) but rather in deep subcortical structures like the hypothalamus and brain stem. We propose that this discrepancy reflects a fundamental algorithmic division in the vertebrate brain between a "learning subsystem" and a "steering subsystem." The learning subsystem (cortex, striatum, and cerebellum) scales via the replication of repetitive modules to maximize computational capacity, analogous to scaling up parameters in machine learning models. By contrast, the steering subsystem (hypothalamus, pallidum, and brainstem) scales via diversification of bespoke cell types to encode innate drives and reflexes, functioning as a high-dimensional biological "reward function." This framework explains the divergence in how evolution has influenced these subsystems and offers a unified lens for understanding brain architecture and the etiology of brain disease; furthermore, it may inform model designs for artificial intelligence.

papers.abstract: Somatic mosaicism is increasingly recognized as a fundamental feature of human biology, yet the detection of somatic mutations remains challenging. The Somatic Mosaicism across Human Tissues (SMaHT) Network conducted large-scale benchmarking experiments involving cell lines and donor tissues to evaluate sequencing technologies, experimental approaches, and computational methods for detecting different types of somatic mutations, generating community resources with >1,000× short-read and 100-400× long-read data for nine analyzed samples. We determined effective strategies for utilizing short- and long-read sequencing for mutation detection and demonstrated that using donor-specific and pangenome-inferred diploid assemblies improved calling, extending mutation catalogs to challenging genomic regions. We benchmarked six duplex technologies and showed that single-cell sequencing resolves cell-type-specific mutational patterns and heterogeneity. Our results indicate that bulk, single-cell, and duplex analyses are complementary and that leveraging all three provides comprehensive characterization of mosaicism within tissues. Together, these findings provide the scientific and clinical communities with a roadmap for accurate genome-wide somatic mutation analysis.

papers.abstract: Clinical proton dose prescription uses a fixed relative biological effectiveness (RBE) factor of 1.1 despite preclinical and clinical evidence that RBE varies with dose, radiation quality, and tissue radiosensitivity, particularly near the distal edge of treatments. We present a proton clinical dose-prescription system which: (1) is consistent with the clinical RBE of 1.1 for target dose definition, (2) uses full microdosimetric spectral distributions including primary and secondary ions, and (3) accounts for RBE variations in a framework analogous to that clinically used in carbon ion radiotherapy. Monte Carlo simulations were performed using OpenTOPAS. The clinical dose was defined as the product of the absorbed dose, the biological RBE calculated with the Mayo Clinic Florida microdosimetric kinetic model (MCF MKM) relative to the mid of a reference 2 Gy (RBE) spread-out Bragg peak, and a clinical scaling factor. The clinical dose system was evaluated across various dose levels, target depths, and spread-out Bragg peak widths. The results were compared with calculations using the fixed RBE factor and two approaches based on dose-averaged linear energy transfer of protons only (Beltran and McNamara models). Across the investigated scenarios, the target-averaged MCF MKM-based RBE ranged from 1.08 to 1.18. The corresponding target-averaged RBE values obtained with the McNamara and the Beltran model were typically 1% lower (range, 86%-105%) and 9% higher (range, 103%-122%), respectively. For all models, substantially higher RBE values were observed at the distal edge and out-of-field. This work establishes a clinical dose system for proton radiotherapy inspired by corresponding Japanese system for carbon ions. The proposed approach maintains consistency with historical proton practice based on a fixed RBE of 1.1 and accounts for the spatial variations of the radiation quality using microdosimetric distributions that include all primary and secondary ions.

papers.abstract: Despite the high risk of postoperative motor dysfunction from corticospinal tract (CST) involvement, no preoperative system integrates CST-tumor interactions to stratify the prognosis in brainstem gliomas (BSGs). We enrolled 180 BSG patients who underwent craniotomy between 2020 and 2023. Preoperative DTI tractography classified CST-tumor relationships as displacement, infiltration, and traverse types. Clinical, pathological, and follow-up data (KPS, mRS, MRC, OS) were systematically collected at predefined intervals. Longitudinal outcomes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models; survival was assessed by Kaplan-Meier. The cohort comprised 51 displacement (28.3%), 83 infiltration (46.1%), and 46 traverse (25.6%) cases, with excellent inter-rater reliability (κ = 0.93). Tumor biology, CST fractional anisotropy (FA), and preoperative functional status demonstrated clear gradients across subtypes. The traverse type was predominantly high-grade (97.8%), exhibited the lowest FA (0.424 ± 0.055), and had the poorest preoperative KPS/mRS (all P < 0.001). Conversely, the displacement type was mostly low-grade (74.5%), showed the highest FA (0.45 ± 0.038), and had superior functional status; infiltration was intermediate. FA correlated positively with preoperative muscle strength (ρ = 0.238, P = 0.001). Longitudinal trajectories differed significantly (P_FDR < 0.05): displacement patients recovered rapidly, traverse patients showed minimal recovery with late decline, and infiltration was intermediate. Median OS was not reached for displacement, versus 15.3 months for infiltration and 12.0 months for traverse; all pairwise comparisons were significant. This DTI-based CST-tumor classification system effectively stratifies BSG patients preoperatively and is associated with distinct recovery trajectories, providing a hypothesis-generating framework for surgical planning.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background Accurate preoperative identification of high-grade dysplasia (HGD) or malignancy in intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs) remains challenging using conventional guideline-based imaging criteria. Quantitative computed tomography (CT)-based features may detect subtle structural changes preceding overt radiologic findings. This study aimed to evaluate whether the pancreatic index (PI) and additional three-dimensional CT-derived quantitative features improve prediction of HGD or malignancy in IPMNs. Methods This single-center retrospective study included patients who underwent surgical resection for pathologically confirmed IPMNs between January 2001 and August 2024 and had available preoperative pancreas-protocol CT. Three-dimensional quantitative parameters were analyzed. Results Among 333 patients, 204 had low-grade dysplasia (LGD), 56 had HGD, and 73 had malignancy. PI decreased with increasing histologic grade (75.6 ± 10.2% in LGD, 74.5 ± 12.0% in HGD, 70.5 ± 12.6% in malignancy; p = 0.003). Pancreatic Hounsfield unit standard deviation (HU-SD) was significantly higher in HGD and malignancy than in LGD (25.6 ± 5.9, 29.0 ± 8.7, and 29.6 ± 6.2, respectively; p < 0.001). A combined model integrating guideline-based criteria with PI, CI, cystic HU-SD, pancreatic HU-SD, and pancreatic duct volume demonstrated better discrimination than the guideline-only model (area under the curve 0.800 vs. 0.760; p = 0.007). Conclusions Quantitative CT-derived imaging features provide incremental value for predicting HGD and malignancy when integrated with conventional guideline-based criteria. These noninvasive imaging biomarkers may enhance risk stratification and provide additional information to support clinical decision-making when integrated with conventional criteria. Further external validation is required to establish their clinical utility in routine practice.

papers.abstract: To evaluate the impact of adjuvant chemotherapy on oncologic outcomes in patients with surgically staged 2009 FIGO stage I uterine serous carcinoma (USC) and to assess the prognostic significance of peritoneal cytology. We retrospectively reviewed patients who underwent surgery at our institution for newly diagnosed, 2009 FIGO stage I USC. Outcomes were stratified by depth of myometrial invasion. We identified 327 patients: 185 (56.6%) with non-myoinvasive disease, 113 (34.6%) with <50% myometrial invasion, and 29 (8.9%) with ≥50% myometrial invasion. Among patients with any myoinvasion, the 5-year PFS was 54.4% (95% CI: 35%-70.2%) for no chemotherapy versus 62.6% (95% CI: 52.2%-71.3%) for chemotherapy (P = 0.10), and the 5-year OS was 52.3% (95% CI: 33.4%-68.2%) versus 79.9% (95% CI: 70.4%-86.6%), respectively (P = 0.008). Use of chemotherapy was independently associated with improved PFS (adjusted HR, 0.50 [95% CI: 0.26-0.96]) and OS (adjusted HR, 0.42 [95% CI: 0.23-0.78]). For patients with non-myoinvasive disease and negative cytology, the 5-year PFS was 89.5% (95% CI: 83.4%-93.5%), and for those with positive cytology, it was 48.8% (95% CI: 22.8%-70.6%; HR, 0.19 [95% CI: 0.08-0.44]). In this patient cohort, postoperative adjuvant chemotherapy was associated with improved survival when myoinvasion was present but did not appear to confer a survival benefit in the absence of myoinvasion. Malignant peritoneal cytology was strongly prognostic in non-myoinvasive disease, and these patients had outcomes resembling those with myoinvasive tumors. These findings support incorporating cytology status into adjuvant decision-making for stage I USC.

papers.abstract: The survival outcomes of advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer (EC) have not improved markedly despite the expanding therapeutic options. We performed molecular characterization of EC to identify therapeutic targets and prognostic biomarkers. Whole-exome sequencing (WES)-based somatic mutation profiling was performed in tumor samples obtained from 67 EC patients (41 early-stage and 26 advanced/recurrent cases). The frequencies of somatic mutations were compared between early and advanced/recurrent EC. Copy number variation analysis was also performed. Survival outcomes and recurrences according to mutational status were analyzed. TP53 and KRAS mutations tended to be more frequent in advanced/recurrent disease than early-stage EC. Deletions were also more common in advanced EC (42.3% vs. 17.1%). Among the advanced EC patients (n=26), 16 patients recurred. Recurrent cases had significantly higher TP53 mutation rates (56.3% versus 10%) and lower PTEN mutation rates (25% versus 80%) than non-recurrent cases. KRAS and CTNNB1 mutations also tended to be enriched. Although KRAS mutation alone only showed a trend of shorter OS (p=0.179) in advanced EC, KRAS-TP53 co-mutation exhibited the worst survival outcomes (p=0.011). KRAS-TP53 co-mutation was associated with chemoresistance: all the co-mutated cases were chemoresistant, whereas patients without either mutation were chemosensitive. Among copy-number low (CNL) and microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) tumors (n=46), KRAS-TP53 co-mutation was strongly associated with adverse survival outcomes (p=0.003). KRAS-TP53 co-mutation represents a potential molecular biomarker of poor prognosis and chemoresistance in advanced EC. It may enable refinement of TCGA classification, especially for CNL and MSI-H subgroups, and support investigation of KRAS-targeted therapeutic strategies.

papers.abstract: Globally, Japan has the largest proportion of individuals aged ≥ 85 years. However, epidemiological studies on cancer in this age group are limited. This study aimed to investigate cancer trends and characteristics among the oldest-old adults (aged ≥ 85 years) in Japan, using population-based national and prefectural cancer registry data on incidence, mortality, trends, stage, and treatment patterns, and compared them with those of young-old adults (aged 65-84 years). From 1995 to 2020, the number of cancer cases among the oldest-old increased more than four-fold, with a significant average annual percent change of +5.9% (confidence interval: 5.4-6.3), surpassing growth in both the overall and young-old populations, and accounting for 15.7% of all cases in 2020. The oldest-old showed higher proportions of skin and gallbladder/bile duct cancers, and rising proportions of breast and prostate cancers. The group was more likely to be diagnosed at unstaged or advanced stages of cancer. Aggressive treatment was less commonly administered to this group, even when the stage at diagnosis was similar to that in the younger-old patients. These findings highlight distinct epidemiological and clinical cancer trends in the oldest-old. Since cancer incidence among the oldest-old will likely continue to rise, targeted healthcare and policy interventions that consider the impact of this age group at both individual and societal levels are urgently needed. To address the needs of an aging population, reconsideration of prevention, detection, and management, including guidelines and specialist availability, is suggested. Moreover, Japan must consider further cancer research in this rapidly increasing population.

papers.abstract: We conducted a controlled trial among 5626 early adolescent women vaccinated in 2007-2009 against human papillomavirus (HPV) types 16/18 to evaluate the impact of high-intensity versus low-intensity cervical screening, respectively at ages 22/25/28 and 28 years with squamous-cell intraepithelial lesions (SILs) as the end-point. The low-intensity cervical screening was non-inferior to the high-intensity screening in the identification of these lesions. Possibly, the transition from cervical infections with vaccine-covered HPV types to infections with non-vaccine-covered HPV types contributes to more manageable occurrence of the screen-detected cervical lesions. Reduction of cervical screening among vaccinated women to a minimum may be warranted to balance the harm-benefit ratio of screening.

papers.abstract: Somatic mosaicism is widespread in human biology and disease, yet robust benchmarks are scarce. The Somatic Mosaicism across Human Tissues (SMaHT) Consortium mixed six HapMap cell lines to create artificial somatic variants spanning 0.25%-16.5% variant allele fractions. We developed a technology-agnostic method that builds pangenome graphs from individual assemblies to create unified benchmarking sets: >6 million single-nucleotide variants, >1.8 million small insertions/deletions, >49,000 structural variations, and 10,000 mobile element insertions across autosomes and mitochondrial chromosomes. We validated the variants using ultra-deep simulated reads and developed a binomial-based model to estimate coverage requirements for variant detection. Evaluating multiple callers showed that telomere-to-telomere CHM13 alignment improves structural variant detection and offers advantages in difficult-to-map regions compared to GRCh38. Low-allele-fraction variant detection remained particularly challenging in repeat-rich genomic regions and falsely duplicated genes. This accurate, versatile resource enables systematic evaluation of somatic variant detection technologies.

papers.abstract: Mosaic mutations in normal tissues occur at low variant allele fractions (VAFs), complicating detection. To benchmark variant-calling strategies, the SMaHT Network created a cell-line mixture (1:49) and produced ultra-deep short- and long-read whole-genome sequencing data across five centers (170×-470× per center). We assembled a reference set of mosaic SNVs and indels, cross-validated with long-read data to expose short-read limitations. We also partitioned the genome by mappability to examine the impact of genomic context, added a negative reference set, and accounted for culture-derived mutations. When seven institutions applied twelve pipelines, callsets were largely discordant across tools and replicates, partly reflecting stochastic sampling of low-VAF mutations in biological replicates. For SNVs with VAFs above 2%, sensitivity and precision approached 80% at ≥300×, with little gain from additional sequencing. This work establishes a framework and best practices for reliably detecting low-VAF mutations in non-cancer tissues and provides a valuable resource for the community.

papers.abstract: Accurate identification of immunogenic neoantigens remains a bottleneck in personalized cancer vaccine development, particularly in low-mutation-burden tumors such as pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). We developed NeoBridge, a hybrid ensemble integrating gradient boosting and a deep neural network across four biologically grounded feature dimensions: HLA binding and processing, differential agretopicity, tumor neoantigen abundance, and TCR recognition potential. Trained on 11,188 experimentally validated neoantigens, NeoBridge achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) of 0.904 on held-out data, with cross-cancer generalization (AUC: 0.73-0.82), including 0.82 in pancreatic cancer, and outperformed established tools. Differential agretopicity emerged as the dominant predictive feature. In 118 PDAC patients with resolved phylogenies and complete follow up, subclonal neoantigen load was associated with worse progression-free survival (p < 0.001) and overall survival (p = 0.038). These findings are hypothesis generating and require prospective immunopeptidomic and functional validation.

papers.abstract: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) occupies a privileged position at the intersection of cellular bioenergetics, redox homeostasis, and signal transduction. Beyond its canonical role in ATP synthesis, NAD serves as an obligate cofactor for enzymes including poly(ADP-ribose) polymerases (PARPs), sirtuins, and CD38, thereby regulating DNA repair, epigenetic remodeling, and inflammatory signaling. Thus, NAD metabolism supports the preservation of cellular homeostasis against oncogenic insults. Malignant transformation, however, imposes substantial biosynthetic and genotoxic stress, often driving metabolic adaptations that amplify NAD production via nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT). This endows cancer cells with enhanced proliferative capacity, stress tolerance, and immunoevasive features. Importantly, the dependence of malignant cells on sustained NAD availability constitutes a therapeutically exploitable vulnerability. Accordingly, NAMPT inhibitors, PARP inhibitors, and strategies targeting NAD-consuming ectoenzymes have shown preclinical and, in select settings, clinical efficacy. Here, we critically review the rewiring of NAD metabolism in cancer, associated therapeutic opportunities, and barriers to their clinical exploitation.

papers.abstract: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has been shown to be beneficial in persons with type 1 diabetes and others with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes, but its role in the treatment of persons with type 2 diabetes not being treated with insulin has needed further study. In a 26-week trial conducted at 22 primary care practices in the United States, we randomly assigned adults with type 2 diabetes who were not using insulin to either CGM or routine care (control). The primary outcome was the glycated hemoglobin level at 26 weeks. Key CGM-measured secondary outcomes were tested hierarchically to control the type I error rate. A total of 145 participants were assigned to the CGM group, and 138 to the routine-care group. Participants ranged in age from 21 to 84 years. The mean (±SD) glycated hemoglobin level decreased from 8.8±1.3% at baseline to 7.2±1.1% at 26 weeks in the CGM group and from 8.7±1.2% to 8.0±1.4% in the routine-care group (adjusted mean difference, -0.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.1 to -0.6; P<0.001). The mean percentage of time that the CGM-measured glucose level was in the glucose-level range of 70 to 180 mg per deciliter was 21 percentage points higher (95% CI, 16 to 26) with CGM than with routine care (P<0.001). The between-group difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 54 mg per deciliter was -0.17 percentage points (95% CI, -0.27 to -0.11; P<0.001 for noninferiority); the difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 70 mg per deciliter was -0.20 percentage points (95% CI, -0.43 to -0.09; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P = 0.004 for superiority). No severe hypoglycemia events were reported. Among adults with type 2 diabetes that was not being treated with insulin and was being managed in a primary care setting, the use of CGM led to a greater reduction in the glycated hemoglobin level and to a lower risk of hyperglycemia than routine care. papers.abstract: Despite growing interest in the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in medicine, empirical evidence on how clinicians use these tools is limited. To characterize clinician use of an AI-enabled clinical information platform, the distribution of use across the clinical workforce, and the purpose of submitted queries. This cross-sectional study analyzed clinicians with National Provider Identifier-verified accounts of a commonly used AI-enabled clinical information platform, OpenEvidence, from January 1, 2024, through June 30, 2026. A large language model was used to classify the clinical purpose and topic areas of a stratified random sample of 38.8 million queries. The number of active users and clinical queries, the share of queries relative to representation in the national workforce, and the clinical purpose and topic of queries were examined. Overall, 952 008 clinicians (58.5% female), including 556 200 physicians, submitted 271 million queries during the 2.5-year study period. Monthly active users increased from 355 in January 2024 to 703 265 in June 2026, and average monthly queries per active user rose from 18.0 to 39.5. Nurse practitioners (44.5) and physician assistants (44.5) submitted more queries per active user-month than physicians (37.1). A higher share of queries relative to the national workforce was submitted by physicians within a decade of graduation (use ratio, 2.54) and residents and fellows (1.84). Use was also higher than average among physicians specializing in oncology and hematology (use ratio, 2.00), internal medicine (1.88), and family medicine (1.80), but lower in procedural and diagnostic specialties (ophthalmology, 0.23; radiology, 0.24; orthopedics, 0.24). Most queries addressed clinical decision-making (51.9%), particularly treatment and management (33.1%), whereas diagnosis accounted for 13.9% of queries. Queries addressing topics outside physicians' own specialties ranged from 35% among oncologists and hematologists to 88% among emergency department physicians. Over 2.5 years, more than 950 000 US clinicians submitted greater than 270 million queries to an AI-enabled clinical information platform. Use varied across clinician types, specialties, and career stages and was frequently for treatment decisions rather than diagnostic tasks.

papers.abstract: Coleoid cephalopods exhibit the highest levels of adenosine deaminases acting on RNA (ADAR)-mediated RNA editing of any known taxon, yet the functional consequences of most recoding events remain unclear. Here, we integrated proteomics with biochemical and cellular assays to characterize recoding across the Doryteuthis pealeii proteome. This confirmed the translation of 7,997 recoded sites at the protein level and revealed how recoding reshapes the proteome by altering protein stability, subcellular localization, post-translational modifications, and enzymatic activity. We find that recoding also creates or ablates post-translational modification sites, with direct effects on protein function and protein-protein interactions. Recoding the E3 ligase MARCHF5 drives widespread changes in substrate ubiquitylation and perturbs mitochondrial homeostasis, illustrating how RNA editing can influence organelle function. Together, these data give a proteome-scale view of how extensive RNA recoding diversifies protein function in coleoid cephalopods and offer a framework for understanding how RNA-level plasticity shapes protein function and cellular physiology.

papers.abstract: Ferroptosis is implicated as a vulnerability in multiple cancers, yet approaches for effectively inducing ferroptosis in vivo are limited. Bypassing conventional strategies targeting the antiferroptotic glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) and ferroptosis suppressor protein 1 (FSP1) proteins, we designed metabolic initiators of lipid peroxidation (MILPOs) and developed the compounds WMK-1/2, which contain tetraoxane radical-generating and mitochondria-targeting groups, as de novo ferroptosis inducers. WMK-1 localizes primarily to mitochondria, induces local lipid peroxidation, and impairs oxidative phosphorylation. WMK-1 induces a "mito-ferroptosis" sub-pathway that skips GPX4 inhibition as a prerequisite, can be rescued by lipophilic radical-trapping antioxidants, yet is minimally sensitive to acyl-coenzyme A synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4) perturbation and long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) supplementation, and evades retinol-mediated protection. Instead, WMK-1-induced cell death requires labile Fe2+ and can be selectively suppressed by ɑ-lipoic acid, an endogenous, mitochondria-resident antioxidant. WMK-1/2 are bioavailable and exhibit significant efficacy in tumor suppression by eliciting ferroptosis in multiple cancer models and augmenting the antitumor effects of immune-checkpoint blockers. Our work provides a protein-targeting-independent metabolic ferroptosis induction strategy for potential cancer therapy.

papers.abstract: Structural variants (SVs) are large (>50 base pairs) genomic rearrangements that can significantly influence human phenotypes, yet their contribution to health and disease remains undercharacterized. We conducted a phenome-wide association study (PheWAS) of 1.6 million SVs identified in whole-genome sequencing data from 467,152 UK Biobank participants, across 13,322 binary, 2,018 quantitative, and 2,923 plasma protein traits. Of these, 82.25% of SVs were outside the detectable range of prior copy-number variant studies. Protein quantitative trait loci analysis linked 3,467 SVs to 1,690 proteins, with effects dependent on SV type and location. In SV-PheWAS, we detected 28,184 associations with human health outcomes. Notably, we uncovered rare SVs with strong phenotypic effects. Furthermore, we show that at known genome-wide association study loci, 32.21% of associated SVs overlapped functional genomic regions. This study underscores the underestimated role of SVs in human genetics and their potential to advance understanding of human biology and drug discovery.

papers.abstract: Coral reefs are diverse marine ecosystems that provide ecological functions and economic and social benefits across over 100 tropical countries. Warming driven by climate change is a primary threat to coral reefs and is increasing the frequency of global coral bleaching events. Here we reassessed the IUCN Red List status of 892 reef-building coral species, first assessed in 2008 1. Because species-level population trends are unavailable for most reef-building corals, population reductions were inferred using proxies based on global coral cover trends and projected annual severe bleaching under SSP2-4.5, both over three decades, adjusted using trait-based estimates of species vulnerability. Of the 774 species with sufficient data to be assessed, 340 (44%) were classified as threatened under IUCN Red List criteria. Thirty-three species were assessed as Critically Endangered, 251 as Endangered, and 56 as Vulnerable, most due to risk of population reduction associated with projected thermal stress. These findings predate the three hottest years on record and the fourth global coral bleaching event (2023-2025), and the first exceedance for an annual mean of the 1.5oC global warming threshold. The findings reinforce the importance of limiting further warming to maintain coral biodiversity and reef ecosystem function. The Red List assesses the relative extinction risk of species, whereby species are placed in categories of increasing risk by comparing their population size, decline and geographic range against standardised thresholds. The Red List does not predict whether or when a species may go extinct. As the ranges of coral species remain under-surveyed, future assessments would be strengthened by species-level population data and thermal-stress and recovery metrics that better capture range-representative dynamics.

papers.abstract: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) remains incurable despite recent therapeutic advances. [177Lu]Lu-PSMA RLT (lutetium-177 labelled prostate-specific membrane antigen radioligand therapy) provides meaningful clinical benefit in selected patients. However, ∼30% of the patients do not respond to [177Lu]Lu-PSMA RLT. Although several baseline prognostic factors are well known, reliable pretherapeutic predictive biomarkers are still lacking. We developed and compared several predictive machine learning (ML) models integrating clinical, biochemical, and imaging data, including [68Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET (gallium-68 labelled prostate-specific membrane antigen ligand positron emission tomography) radiomic features, to estimate overall survival (OS) in patients with mCRPC treated with [177Lu]Lu-PSMA RLT. This retrospective monocentric study included 102 patients with mCRPC treated with [177Lu]Lu-PSMA between January 2022 and March 2024. Five lesions per patient were segmented on their pretherapeutic [68Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET/computed tomography (CT) scans. Radiomic features were extracted following Image Biomarker Standardization Initiative guidelines. Multimodal ML models integrating clinical, genomic, biochemical, and imaging features (including radiomics) were developed to predict OS. Median OS of the total cohort was 11.2 mo. Intralesional homogeneity, characterized by the second-order radiomic feature normalized inverse difference moment, was associated with shorter OS (p = 0.025). The best-performing ML model achieved a 12-mo area under the curve (AUC) of 0.778 by combining 22 clinical, biochemical, genomic, and radiomic features. The model leveraging PET data alone achieved strong performance, with an AUC comparable to the clinical model (0.715 vs 0.766). ML models based on [68Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT, including radiomic features, offer a noninvasive, standardized, and widely accessible approach to predict OS in patients with mCRPC treated with [177Lu]Lu-PSMA RLT. This study highlights the strong predictive potential of PSMA PET imaging for patient stratification in a real-world setting.

papers.abstract: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) regulate multiple mechanisms associated with glioblastoma (GBM) therapy resistance, which remains a major challenge in GBM treatment. Some resistance mechanisms involve genetic heterogeneity, glioblastoma stem cells, the tumor microenvironment, autophagy, metabolic reprogramming, vascular adaptation, and altered transcriptional regulation. By regulating protein activity, stability, localization, interactions, and signaling, PTMs can influence several of these processes and affect treatment response. This review examines the roles of phosphorylation, ubiquitination and ubiquitin-like modifications, acetylation, methylation, and glycosylation in resistance to temozolomide, radiotherapy, and targeted therapies. We further discuss emerging PTMs, including lactylation, succinylation, and UFMylation, for which evidence linking individual modifications to therapeutic resistance ranges from direct resistance mechanisms to effects primarily associated with GBM biology. PTM crosstalk is also discussed in the context of DNA repair, redox homeostasis, metabolism, glioblastoma stem cell maintenance, and therapy response. Finally, we examine pharmacological targeting of PTM-regulating enzymes and pathways and the effects of natural bioactive compounds on PTM-dependent mechanisms.

papers.abstract: Aim LGALS3BP (also known as Galectin-3-binding protein, Gal-3BP, or 90 K) is a multifunctional secreted glycoprotein involved in tumor progression and has emerged as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target in several malignancies, including neuroblastoma (NB). Increasing evidence suggests that LGALS3BP contributes to shaping the NB tumor microenvironment (TME), particularly through its enrichment on tumor-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs), where it may regulate tumor-stroma interplay. We investigated whether LGALS3BP contributes to stromal cell modulation in NB and is associated with changes in EV cargo composition. Methods A patient-derived NB cell line naturally lacking LGALS3BP (hNB CTRL) and a matched counterpart ectopically re-expressing LGALS3BP (hNB LGALS3BP) were used. Bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMMSCs) were exposed to NB-derived conditioned media (CM) to assess cytokine secretion and LGALS3BP detection in recipient cells. EV cargo was analyzed by microRNA (miRNA) and proteomic profiling. Selected candidates were validated by qPCR and immunoblotting on NB-derived EVs. Proteomic analysis revealed enrichment of RNA-binding proteins, including SRSF1, in LGALS3BP-EVs. papers.abstract: To determine whether plasma and serum extracellular vesicles (EV) are interchangeable for immunoaffinity-enriched proteomic profiling in high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC), and whether an EV protein signature improves diagnostic performance beyond CA-125 for detecting ovarian cancer. We performed immunoaffinity-enriched proteomic profiling of EV subpopulations from 243 paired EDTA plasma and serum samples in a nested case-control cohort from the UK Ovarian Cancer Population Study (controls, benign, borderline, and HGSOC). Analyses assessed proteomic depth, plasma-serum concordance, and diagnostic performance using machine learning. Plasma-derived EV subpopulations showed greater proteomic depth than serum, with 6439 versus 5451 protein groups identified and 2838 versus 840 proteins detected at 50% prevalence. Protein intensities were highly concordant between matrices (r = 0.86, p < 0.001), maintained across disease groups and cancer stages. For distinguishing HGSOC from non-cancers, an EV-augmented CA-125 model achieved an AUROC of 0.97 in plasma and 0.96 in serum, improving plasma sensitivity to 99% (95% CI 89-100) and specificity to 85% (95% CI 68-91) versus 96% (95% CI 82-100) sensitivity and 65% (95% CI 15-73) specificity for CA-125 alone, with similarly high discrimination in serum. Surface epitope-targeted EV subpopulation enrichment yields specific proteomic profiling of HGSOC with highly concordant biomarker signatures across plasma and serum, supporting their interchangeable use in clinical and biobank settings. The EV-augmented CA-125 model outperformed CA-125 alone, with recurrent EV proteins reflecting mucin-mediated immune evasion, and metabolic reprogramming, underscoring the translational potential of this approach for blood-based ovarian cancer detection.

papers.abstract: T-cell exhaustion limits durable antitumor responses and remains a barrier to adoptive cell therapies (ACT) in solid tumors. To identify regulators of T-cell persistence, we performed genome-wide CRISPR knockout screens in primary human CD8⁺ T cells expressing an NY-ESO-1-specific T-cell receptor and subjected them to repeated tumor cell rechallenge. These screens revealed enrichment of single-guide RNAs targeting components of Cullin-RING E3 ligases, particularly Cullin-5 (CRL5) assemblies comprising CUL5, RNF7, and ARIH2. Disruption of CRL5 genes in T cells preserved cytotoxic activity and enhanced cytokine production while sustaining effector-associated transcriptional programs and suppressing exhaustion-related signatures. Pharmacologic inhibition of cullin neddylation with the NEDD8-activating enzyme inhibitor MLN4924 recapitulated CRL5 loss and enhanced T-cell effector function in vitro. In a human melanoma xenograft model, ACT with CRL5-deficient T cells improved tumor control. Together, these findings identify CRL5 as a negative regulator of T-cell fitness and a potential therapeutic target to enhance ACT durability in solid tumors.

papers.abstract: Engineered T-cell therapies are limited by progressive dysfunction under chronic tumor antigen exposure, and genetic perturbation of negative regulators has emerged as a promising strategy to sustain effector activity. We reanalyzed a genome-wide CRISPR knockout screen in primary human T cells under repetitive tumor stimulation; protein-protein interaction mapping revealed seven members of the Cullin-RING Ligase 5 (CRL5) complex as an enriched hit cluster. Knockout of any of these members (CUL5, ARIH2, RNF7, UBE2F, UBE2L3, CISH, DCUN1D3) enhanced tumor serial killing, and CUL5, the complex scaffold, emerged as the strongest target. CUL5 knockout T cells exhibited sustained cytotoxicity, elevated effector cytokine production, and fewer exhaustion marker-positive cells while retaining antigen specificity and cytokine dependence. Quantitative ubiquitylation proteomics in resting, and acutely and chronically stimulated T cells mapped CRL5-dependent candidate substrates beyond the canonical JAK/STAT axis, including nutrient transporters, receptor trafficking proteins, and TCR signaling components. The benefit of CUL5 knockout extended across CARs targeting CD19, BCMA, and HER2 with different costimulatory domains, and to 1XX-modified CAR and HLA-independent TCR architectures. Combining CUL5 ablation with a tumor-induced IL-2 circuit produced tumor control across nine rounds of repetitive stimulation, whereas either modification alone eventually failed. In vivo, CUL5 knockout BCMA CAR T cells were enriched in the bone marrow following repeated tumor rechallenge and exhibited enhanced ex vivo cytotoxicity after nearly 90 days in tumor-bearing mice. These findings position CUL5 perturbation as a strategy to improve T-cell persistence and the efficacy of adoptive cell therapies, potentially with engineered cytokine support.

papers.abstract: Alternative lengthening of telomeres (ALT) is a telomerase-independent telomere maintenance mechanism that supports the growth of approximately 5-10% of human tumors and represents an attractive but insufficiently explored therapeutic target. CRISPR-based functional genomics has emerged as a powerful approach to systematically interrogate ALT biology and identify genetic dependencies associated with the ALT state. In this Review, we discuss the CRISPR-based strategies applied to ALT, including hypothesis-driven targeted loss-of-function screens, phenotype-driven optical screens, in silico mining of large-scale dependency datasets, and genome-wide screens in ALT-adjacent states. Across these approaches, recurrent dependencies converge on pathways mediating replication stress buffering, DNA repair, and telomere maintenance, including FANCM, SMARCAL1, and SUB1. Collectively, these findings support a model in which ALT-positive cells rely not on a unique ALT-specific factor, but rather on stress-buffering mechanisms that prevent chronic telomeric dysfunction from triggering replication catastrophe and cell death, highlighting these pathways as promising candidates for further therapeutic investigation.

papers.abstract: Monocyte-to-macrophage differentiation is a central process that shapes immune responses across diverse contexts, yet how inflammatory cues engage metabolism to instruct monocyte fate commitment remains unclear. Here, using a CRISPR-based metabolic screen combined with monocyte-specific perturbations in bacterial lung infection, we identified lactate dehydrogenase A (LDHA) as a key metabolic regulator of monocyte commitment to the nitric oxide synthase 2 (NOS2)+ macrophage fate in vivo. LDHA-dependent cytosolic nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) regeneration enabled selective hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha (HIF1α) translation through its 5' untranslated region (UTR) and is associated with structural remodeling of this region. HIF1α then functioned as a downstream effector that promoted the NOS2+ macrophage fate. Granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) further acted as an upstream metabolic priming signal that enhanced LDHA-dependent HIF1α regulation and supported this differentiation process. Together, these findings suggest that metabolic redox state regulates monocyte fate commitment through selective mRNA translation coupled to RNA structural remodeling.

papers.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a leading cause of disability, and non-invasive stimulation of deep brain circuits such as the subgenual anterior cingulate cortex (sgACC) remains challenging. This randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial recruits 96 adults with moderate-to-severe MDD who received 10 sessions of 2 mA low-current, 15 mA high-current, or sham transcranial temporal interference stimulation (tTIS) targeting the left sgACC. The high-current group shows significantly greater reductions in depressive symptoms (17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale [HDRS-17] score) post-treatment and at 1-month follow-up compared with sham and outperforms the low-current group post-treatment. Exploratory Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) analyses suggest improved sleep quality in both active groups, whereas anxiety outcomes show no intergroup differences. High-current tTIS is safe and well tolerated, with only transient tingling. These findings provide preliminary evidence that sgACC-targeted tTIS relieves depressive symptoms safely, with more robust short-to medium-term effects observed under the 15 mA protocol. This trial registers on Chictr.org.cn (ChiCTR2400094971).

papers.abstract: Mitral valve repair (MVr) is the ideal treatment strategy for degenerative mitral regurgitation. Mitral valve replacement (MVR) may be required if MVr is unsuccessful during the index surgery. The consequences of MVR following failed MVr during the same surgery are unclear. Retrospective observational study. Single institution, university affiliated. All patients who underwent MVR from 2010 through 2024 were included. Patients with concomitant surgeries were included. Patients were dichotomized into the intended repair (IR) or de novo replacement (DR) groups based on the intended procedure. A total of 1,661 patients (mean age, 64 years; 57% female) underwent MVR. MVr was attempted in 133 patients (8%, IR group), and 1,528 underwent planned MVR (92%, DR group). The mean ejection fraction was 55%. Female sex (58.0% in the DR group v 48.9% in the IR group, p = 0.04), history of infective endocarditis (23.8% v 15.0%, p = 0.02), history of cerebrovascular disease (32.1% v 19.5%, p = 0.03), and prior sternotomy (32.1% v 15.8%, p < 0.001) were more prevalent in the DR group. After propensity score matching, perioperative morbidity and mortality were similar. The median cardiopulmonary bypass time and cross-clamp time were longer in the IR group (207 minutes v 134 minutes in the DR group and 163 minutes v 102 minutes in the DR group, respectively). Kaplan-Meier curve analysis showed similar 5-year survival (p = 0.91). Postoperative outcomes were similar despite longer operative times in the IR group. Failure of initial MVr, leading to MVR, did not translate into adverse early or long-term outcomes. These findings suggest that repair may be more aggressively considered in patients with repairable anatomies.

papers.abstract: To evaluate the reliability and readability of responses generated by two artificial intelligence (AI) platforms-ChatGPT and MediSearch-to common patient-focused questions about cardiac surgery and its anesthetic implications. Prospective, comparative, cross-sectional evaluation. Single-institution academic study; no direct patient involvement. Questions were sourced from publicly available online data (Google "People Also Ask" feature). One hundred unique patient-focused questions about cardiac surgery and anesthesia, categorized using the Rothwell classification system (80 fact, 14 policy, 6 value). Each question was submitted individually to the free versions of ChatGPT (version 4.0) and MediSearch. Responses were evaluated using three validated metrics: reliability, assessed using the modified DISCERN tool; readability, assessed using the Flesch-Kincaid grade level (FK) and Coleman-Liau index (CL); and clinical accuracy, assessed by a board-certified cardiothoracic anesthesiologist and a board-certified cardiothoracic surgeon using a 3-point Likert scale. MediSearch demonstrated significantly higher reliability (mean DISCERN score, 4.64 v 2.47; p < 0.001). ChatGPT generated significantly more readable responses (mean FK score, 10.33 v 11.34 [p < 0.01]; mean CL score, 15.72 v 17.30 [p < 0.001]) and significantly higher clinical accuracy (mean, 0.82 v 0.71; p < 0.01). Subgroup analysis by Rothwell category confirmed MediSearch's reliability advantage across all question types, while ChatGPT's readability advantage was most pronounced for fact-based questions. This study reveals a critical trade-off between evidence-based reliability and linguistic accessibility in AI-generated cardiac surgery patient education content. MediSearch offers superior reliability, while ChatGPT provides more readable and accurate responses. Neither platform achieves the sixth-grade readability level recommended for broad public accessibility. These findings underscore the need for AI platforms to balance clinical accuracy with health literacy standards before being endorsed as patient education tools in high-stakes settings.

papers.abstract: Diaphragmatic dysfunction contributes to perioperative respiratory morbidity. Point-of-care ultrasound enables noninvasive bedside assessment of diaphragmatic structure and motion and is increasingly used in perioperative practice. However, its diagnostic performance and measurement reliability in this setting have not been systematically evaluated. This scoping review aimed to map the available evidence, with emphasis on reliability, reproducibility, and agreement with reference standards. A scoping review was conducted in accordance with Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and reported as per Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews. A protocol was registered on the Open Science Framework. MEDLINE, MEDLINE ePubs and In-Process Citations, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane databases were searched. Eligible studies included adult or paediatric surgical patients undergoing perioperative diaphragmatic ultrasound. Data were charted on study characteristics, ultrasound techniques, reference standards, and measures of diagnostic accuracy and inter- and intra-observer agreement. Nineteen studies (712 patients) were included, most being prospective observational and published after 2015. In adults, diaphragmatic ultrasound showed generally positive, although variable, correlations with spirometry, transdiaphragmatic pressure, electrophysiological measures, neuromuscular recovery, and arterial blood gas-based weaning criteria. Thresholds for excursion and thickening varied across studies. Inter- and intra-observer agreement was generally good to excellent, including among operators with limited training. In paediatric populations, ultrasound demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy and strong agreement with fluoroscopy, with excellent interobserver reliability. Perioperative diaphragmatic ultrasound shows acceptable reliability and agreement with reference standards. Heterogeneity in techniques and outcomes limits comparability. Standardisation and outcome-linked studies are needed to define its role.

papers.abstract: Self-organization generates cellular patterns that guide morphogenesis, but how it regulates collective cell fate remains underexplored. We show that cellular self-organization constrains the propagation of ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of oxidative cell death that can otherwise spread as unbounded trigger waves. The spatial patterning of cell density and alignment encodes transcriptional programs, priming cells toward ferroptosis-sensitive or -resistant fates. Low-density, misaligned regions with elevated YAP/TEAD1 activity are sensitive, whereas high-density, aligned regions with increased NRF2 expression form propagation-resistant boundaries. Cell elongation establishes a polarized distribution of oxidizable lipids, creating peroxidation hotspots at the cell poles that promote propagation along cell alignment. In silico and pharmacological perturbations reveal that pattern-dependent susceptibility and polarized lipid organization act together to constrain isotropic waves into spatially confined, anisotropic propagation. These findings identify self-organization as a systems-level mechanism governing collective homeostasis, providing a paradigm to explore how tissue-scale organization regulates cell death in development and disease.

papers.abstract: The mu-opioid receptor (MOR) is a major target for pain treatment, but its effectiveness is limited by dangerous side effects. However, the systemic administration of opioids makes it difficult both to decipher their underlying mechanisms of action and to limit drug action to specific receptor subpopulations to isolate therapeutic effects from adverse effects. Here, we develop a reversibly photoswitchable morphinan agonist termed "azo-morphine-3" (AM-3) that interconverts from low to high efficacy in response to light to enable optical control of MOR signaling. Structural analysis of the low ("trans") and high ("cis") efficacy states of AM-3 bound to the MOR reveals distinct binding modes, with each state driving unique ligand, receptor, and G protein dynamics. In mice, AM-3 drives reversible and repeatable optical control of antinociception across pain models with a reduced side effect profile owing to its limited brain accumulation and its ability to be locally activated.

papers.abstract: Exercise reduces all-cause mortality, yet its molecular effects across organs, sexes, and circadian phases remain incompletely understood. We subjected mice to 8 weeks of voluntary wheel running and collected 22 tissues and plasma during active and inactive phases for bulk RNA sequencing, metabolomics, proteomics, and single-nucleus RNA and methylation sequencing. Exercise induced canonical fiber-type switching and widespread, tissue-specific remodeling, with the largest transcriptomic changes in skeletal muscle. Except for the hypothalamus, kidney, and lung, most tissues changed more during the active phase. Females showed broader transcriptional responses, with distinct downregulation. Pairing single-nucleus methylomes with transcriptomes resolved the cell types driving exercise-induced epigenetic remodeling-changes undetectable by bulk studies. These included coordinated gene-body demethylation and transcription that tracked with fiber-type switching in specific myonuclei. Cell-type-resolved methylation, including partially methylated domains characterized in muscle, revealed a strong, sex-biased epigenetic response to training. Machine learning identified conserved exercise signatures across mammalian species.

papers.abstract: Transgender women (TGW) retain lifelong prostate cancer (PCa) risk despite gender-affirming hormone therapy (GAHT), yet its association with PCa incidence and severity is poorly synthesised. This study aimed to quantify pooled PCa incidence in TGW on GAHT relative to cisgender men and characterise disease severity. This is a systematic review with meta-analysis per Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews: CRD420261369142). Five databases were searched from inception to April 2026. Eligible studies reported PCa incidence or outcomes in ≥5 TGW or gender-diverse individuals with intact prostates receiving GAHT. Screening, extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment (Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies - of Interventions; JBI) were performed in duplicate. Random-effects meta-analyses pooled standardised incidence ratios (SIR), incidence rates, and proportions with recorded PCa. Nine studies drawn from six independent data sources (54 342 TGW on GAHT; 160 PCa cases) were included. Pooled SIR versus age-adjusted cisgender men was 0.224 (95% confidence interval = 0.146-0.344; κ = 2), a 77.6% relative reduction; pooled incidence rate was 22.9 versus 98.1 per 100 000 person-years. Among 36 cases with reported grade, 33.3% were International Society of Urological Pathology grade group 4-5; prostate-specific antigen (PSA) ranged from 6.5-18.0 ng/ml and was not pooled. Grade and stage data were derived from fewer than 40 patients with no matched cisgender comparison. Detected PCa incidence is substantially lower in TGW receiving GAHT, on very low certainty evidence. Case-level data include a non-negligible proportion of high-grade disease, but whether severity differs from matched cisgender populations remains uncertain. Clinicians should not equate population-level reduction with individual-level protection. Validated PSA thresholds and screening pathways are needed.

papers.abstract: Cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass structurally alters respiratory mechanics and carries a substantial risk of postoperative morbidity. Historically, patients have routinely received conventional oxygen therapy (COT) following extubation. High- flow nasal cannula (HCNC) therapy has emerged as an innovative respiratory support system. By synthesizing all currently available high-quality randomized controlled trials (RCTs), this study aimed to rigorously evaluate the efficacy and safety of HFNC compared to COT, focusing primarily on determining the need for escalation of respiratory support. A thorough electronic search was carried out in the PubMed, Embase, and Scopus databases from their inception to May 2026. Only RCTs were considered for analysis. A random-effects model was applied to compute pooled estimates and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). A total of 11 RCTs, comprising 2473 patients, were included in this systematic review and meta-analysis. HFNC had a statistically significant effect on reducing the requirement for escalation of respiratory support (risk ratio [RR] = 0.71; 95% CI, 0.55-0.93; p = 0.01). HFNC had a statistically significant effect on improving the arterial partial pressure of oxygen, as well as forced expiratory volume in 1 second, while also increasing delirium complications (RR = 3.63; 95% CI, 1.80-7.30; p = 0.0003). There were no statistically significant differences between the 2 approaches in the other secondary clinical and resource utilization outcomes, including intubation, overall mortality, hospital length of stay, intensive care unit length of stay, and postoperative atrial fibrillation. In adult patients recovering from cardiac surgery, HFNC therapy improves oxygenation and significantly curtails the need to escalate respiratory support compared to COT. However, these physiologic and intermediate clinical benefits do not translate into reductions in mortality, reintubation rate, or hospital length of stay and may come at the cost of increased postoperative delirium.

papers.abstract: Breast cancer that arises in the postpartum period often carries a poor prognosis and urgently requires chemoprevention strategies, particularly for women at elevated risk. Here, we report that a single post-lactation dose of cabergoline, a dopaminergic agonist that blocks prolactin secretion, delays the onset and reduces the incidence of postpartum mammary cancer in K14-Cre; Brca1F/F, Trp53F/F mice. In these mice, cabergoline treatment remodels the mammary gland by potentiating involution, reducing ductal area and proliferation, and reversing T cell exhaustion, potentially through modulation of ion channel expression. Notably, independent retrospective studies in two large cohorts of European women showed that cabergoline treatment was associated with a lower incidence of postpartum breast cancer, with a meta-analysis indicating an approximate 69% reduction in risk. Our work underscores the importance of targeting postlactational involution as a strategy for the prevention of postpartum breast cancer and positions cabergoline as a novel, low-risk chemoprevention strategy.

papers.abstract: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) with inferior vena cava (IVC) tumor thrombus is associated with substantial perioperative risk and frequent recurrence despite nephrectomy and thrombectomy. No established neoadjuvant local therapy exists for this high-risk population. To evaluate the feasibility, safety, clinical outcomes, and exploratory biomarker effects of neoadjuvant stereotactic ablative radiotherapy (SABR) targeting IVC tumor thrombus before nephrectomy and thrombectomy. This single-center prospective phase 2 nonrandomized clinical trial enrolled patients with newly diagnosed RCC and Mayo level II to IV IVC tumor thrombus eligible for neoadjuvant SABR and definitive surgery from July 2015 to January 2024. Data were analyzed from August 2025 to August 2026. Neoadjuvant SABR to the radiographically defined IVC tumor thrombus, delivered as 40 Gy in 5 fractions or 36 Gy in 3 fractions, followed by radical nephrectomy and IVC thrombectomy. The primary end point was 1-year recurrence-free survival (RFS) compared with a prespecified historical surgery-alone benchmark of 55.7%. Secondary outcomes included 90-day perioperative morbidity and mortality, adverse events, pulmonary embolism, overall survival, and cancer-specific survival. Exploratory analyses included Ki-67 immunohistochemistry and tumor-informed circulating tumor DNA. Of 23 patients who received neoadjuvant SABR, 22 completed surgery, and 21 were included in the primary RFS analysis. Of 21 included patients, 12 (57%) were male, and the median (IQR) age was 62.5 (54.0-73.2) years. A total of 19 patients had clear-cell RCC; all tumors were grade 3 or 4, and 3 patients had metastatic disease at enrollment. At a median (range) follow-up of 108.6 (2.0-127.2) months, 1-year RFS was 71.4% (80% CI, 56.6-82.0; 95% CI, 47.2-86.0), meeting the prespecified phase 2 screening criterion based on comparison with the historical surgery-alone benchmark of 55.7% (P = .09). One-year overall survival was 95.2% (80% CI, 83.9-98.7; 95% CI, 70.7-99.3) and cancer-specific survival was 95.2% (80% CI, 83.9-98.7; 95% CI, 70.7-99.3). No 90-day perioperative mortality occurred; 4 grade 4 treatment-attributed events occurred, but no grade 4/5 radiation-attributed toxic effects occurred. Ki-67 expression was reduced in patients with irradiated tumor thrombus compared with nonirradiated controls. Tumor-informed circulating tumor DNA was detected in all patients with available plasma and declined after treatment. In this nonrandomized clinical trial, neoadjuvant SABR before nephrectomy and IVC thrombectomy appeared feasible with an acceptable safety profile. RFS met the prespecified phase 2 screening criterion but remains exploratory and warrants further evaluation. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT02473536.

papers.abstract: The exquisite antigen specificity of T cells is one foundation of modern cancer immunotherapy. The therapeutic efficacy of checkpoint blockade, cancer vaccines, and engineered T-cell therapies, all appear to depend on T cells capable of recognizing specific antigens displayed by tumor cells. In a recent issue of Nature Immunology, Smith and colleagues challenge this paradigm by demonstrating that local activation of virus-specific memory T cells can eliminate tumors without direct tumor-cell recognition. Instead, activated T cells initiate a multicellular inflammatory response involving IFNγ, TNF, nitric oxide and recruited myeloid cells that collectively induce tumor-cell death. These findings separate the antigen specificity required for T-cell activation from that required for tumor killing and expand the role of T cells from direct cytotoxic effectors to organizers of a broader antitumor response. Together, these findings broaden the potential scope of T-cell-mediated antitumor immunity beyond the constraints of direct tumor-antigen recognition.

papers.abstract: The primary objective was to evaluate the influence of needle tip positioning during suprazygomatic maxillary nerve block on bupivacaine concentration within the pterygopalatine fossa (PPF). The secondary objective was to correlate early injectate spread on computed tomography (CT) with PPF bupivacaine concentrations. Suprazygomatic maxillary nerve block attempts (n=34) were performed on 17 human cadaveric heads with different needle tip positions. Each attempt involved injection of 5 mL containing 0.4% bupivacaine, iohexol, and methylene blue. Computed tomography was used to determine needle tip location and early injectate spread. PPF samples were harvested via a transmaxillary approach for bupivacaine quantification by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. The highest median [Q1-Q3] bupivacaine concentrations were observed when needle tip was positioned within pterygomaxillary fissure or PPF, with 829.3 [728.1-1015.7] µg/g, and when positioned directly against maxillary tuberosity, with 535.3 [355.7-820.7] µg/g. Concentrations were highly variable with off-bone infratemporal placements (range, 0.1-335.8 µg/g). Lateral needle displacement was associated with lower bupivacaine concentrations (β=-0.193, 95% CI -0.301 to -0.086; P<0.001), whereas anterior (β=0.107, 95% CI 0.018-0.196; P=0.020) and cranial displacement (β=0.079, 95% CI 0.017-0.141; P=0.014) were associated with higher concentrations. CT contrast spread between temporalis and lateral pterygoid muscles was not associated with higher PPF bupivacaine concentrations (P=0.117). Needle tip position influenced bupivacaine concentration within PPF, with concentrations generally increasing as the needle approached PPF and with more anterior positioning, including placement at the maxillary tuberosity. More superficial or posterior infratemporal placements yielded lower and more variable concentrations. Moreover, infratemporal contrast spread on early CT imaging was not associated with higher PPF bupivacaine concentrations.

papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly reshaping anaesthesiology and critical care, enhancing physiological monitoring, perioperative risk prediction, and clinical decision-making. As its adoption accelerates, attention has increasingly turned to the environmental consequences of digital healthcare, raising important questions regarding the energy consumption and carbon footprint associated with clinical AI. This study examines the environmental implications of AI in anaesthesiology and critical care by placing computational emissions within the broader context of healthcare sustainability. Current evidence indicates that, although AI systems generate measurable greenhouse gas emissions, their operational carbon footprint remains several orders of magnitude lower than that of established sources of emissions, including volatile anaesthetic agents, intensive care, and surgical care. Quantitative comparisons, complemented by an illustrative environmental break-even analysis, suggest that even modest improvements in healthcare efficiency may be sufficient to offset the operational emissions of current clinical AI applications. These findings indicate that the sustainability of clinical AI should not be judged solely by its computational footprint, but by its overall environmental value. The relevant question is not simply how much AI emits, but whether its implementation reduces resource utilisation, avoids unnecessary healthcare activities, and generates environmental savings that outweigh its own operational costs. Achieving this objective will require computationally efficient model design, low-carbon digital infrastructures, lifecycle assessment, and the routine integration of environmental metrics into AI evaluation. Rather than representing a major new source of healthcare emissions, clinical AI should be viewed as an opportunity to advance both digital innovation and environmental stewardship. By integrating sustainability alongside clinical effectiveness, anaesthesiologists are uniquely positioned to guide the responsible development and implementation of AI technologies that benefit both patients and the healthcare systems in which they are delivered.

papers.abstract: Gastrodin is a natural compound with anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antitumor activities; however, its therapeutic role and molecular mechanisms in colorectal cancer (CRC) remain unclear. In this study, we explored the anti-CRC mechanisms of gastrodin through integrated bioinformatics and experimental validation. The potential targets of gastrodin were obtained from public databases. Transcriptomic data of CRC were retrieved from TCGA and GEO datasets, and the differentially expressed genes were screened. The CRC-related genes were subjected to gene-set variation analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and the core genes were identified by the LASSO regression, support vector machine, and random forest algorithms, followed by SHAP analysis. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), immune infiltration analysis, consensus clustering, molecular docking, and in vitro experiments were further performed. A total of 628 potential gastrodin targets and 15 overlapping CRC-related genes were identified. Five core hub genes, including NFE2L3, UBE2S, CA9, CCNB1, and CFD, were screened, among which NFE2L3 showed the highest SHAP importance score. The scRNA-seq data indicated cell-type-specific expression patterns of these genes in CRC tissues. Immune infiltration analysis further suggested that gastrodin may regulate the CRC immune microenvironment by regulating the activated B cells, activated CD4⁺ T cells, and other immune cells. Molecular docking revealed favorable binding affinity between gastrodin and the five core proteins. Moreover, NFE2L3 was highly expressed in CRC tissues and cell lines, and its knockdown significantly inhibited the proliferation, migration, and invasion of the tumor cells. Gastrodin may suppress CRC progression by targeting key genes, particularly NFE2L3, and modulating the tumor immune microenvironment. Furthermore, our study has identified the potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for CRC.

papers.abstract: Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab in localized deficient mismatch repair/microsatellite instability-high gastric or gastroesophageal junction (GEJ) adenocarcinoma was evaluated in the NEONIPIGA study. The primary end point of pathological complete response (pCR) was previously reported. To report long-term follow-up results and secondary end points, including event-free survival (EFS) and overall survival (OS), of the NEONIPIGA study. The NEONIPIGA study is a French, multicenter, single-arm, phase 2 nonrandomized clinical trial that included patients with histologically proven cT2-T4NXM0 deficient mismatch repair/microsatellite instability-high GEJ adenocarcinoma who were eligible for surgery. Patients were enrolled between October 23, 2019, and June 4, 2021, and the database was locked on November 13, 2025. Neoadjuvant nivolumab, 240 mg, every 2 weeks for 6 cycles plus ipilimumab, 1 mg/kg, every 6 weeks for 2 cycles, followed by surgery 5 weeks after the last nivolumab dose, and adjuvant nivolumab, 480 mg, every 4 weeks for 9 cycles. EFS and OS. A total of 32 patients (median [range] age, 65 [40-80] years; 8 [28%] female and 21 [72%] were male) were included: 16 (50%) with gastric cancer and 16 (50%) with GEJ cancer. Three patients did not undergo surgery (1 with metastatic disease and 2 who refused). Twenty-seven patients (84%) completed neoadjuvant therapy and 14 (44%) received all treatment as planned. Neoadjuvant and adjuvant therapy-related grade 3/4 adverse events occurred in 6 (19%) and 4 patients (17%), respectively. Median follow-up was 48.3 months (95% CI, 44.8-52.0 months). Among the 32 patients in the intention-to-treat population, 4-year OS was 84.1% (95% CI, 65.8%-93.0%). In the 31 patients eligible for surgery, 4-year EFS was 83.5% (95% CI, 64.8%-92.8%). One patient relapsed with cerebral metastases. Six deaths occurred: 2 related to gastric cancer or treatment (1 patient had postoperative complications and 1 cerebral metastases) and 4 unrelated. All patients who did not undergo surgery achieved a clinical complete response after immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy. One patient subsequently died of causes unrelated to their cancer. Overall, 17 of 29 patients (59%) achieved pCR on surgical specimen. Safety was previously reported, and no additional late toxic effects were observed. In this phase 2 nonrandomized clinical trial, the immunotherapy regimen evaluated was associated with sustained long-term survival, but no clear evidence of improved survival over outcomes reported in other studies evaluating surgery alone in this patient population was observed. The high pCR rates and durable responses observed may provide useful information for designing future clinical studies, including randomized trials investigating organ-preserving strategies. papers.abstract: N- and O-glycosylation are structurally diverse post-translational modifications that affect a range of biological functions. Glycoproteomics faces substantial challenges, particularly in the analysis of O-glycans due to their diversity compared to that of N-glycans. In addition, tandem mass spectrometry data patterns exhibit variability between different fragmentation methods. Existing de novo algorithms often lack sensitivity and are limited to sceHCD fragmentation, restricting their practical application. To address these limitations, we introduce DeepGlycan, a deep-learning-based method for de novo glycopeptide sequencing that captures relationships between glycopeptide spectra and fragment ions from both N- and O-glycans. DeepGlycan achieves over 92% glycan recall and around 95% glycan precision on N-glycopeptide spectra generated using both sceHCD and EThcD. In addition, it enables O-glycan de novo sequencing without additional training. Beyond benchmarking, DeepGlycan identifies an O-glycopeptide in mouse heart tissue whose assignment is supported by exoglycosidase treatment and comparison with a synthetic standard.

papers.abstract: The PfPCRCR complex is essential for invasion of human erythrocytes by the deadliest malaria parasite, Plasmodium falciparum. Antibodies against each subunit of PfPCRCR prevent erythrocyte invasion and the PfRH5 component is currently the most advanced blood-stage malaria vaccine. Central within PfPCRCR is PfRIPR. This complex molecule contains a core and a flexible tail and allows PfPCRCR to bridge the parasite and erythrocyte during invasion. In this study, we generated a small panel of human monoclonal antibodies against PfRIPR. We structurally characterised four PfRIPR tail-binding antibodies in complex with PfRIPR fragments. We show that growth-inhibitory antibody RP.012 induces a kink in the PfRIPR tail while non-inhibitory antibodies do not. Furthermore, we show that these four antibodies modulate each other, either through antagonism or by acting synergistically. These studies have implications for the design of PfRIPR-based vaccine immunogens and indicate that the tail of PfRIPR undergoes essential conformational changes during erythrocyte invasion.

papers.abstract: The crawling motility of nematode sperm is driven by the unconventional cytoskeletal protein, Major Sperm Protein (MSP). In developing spermatocytes, MSP assembles on the cytosolic side of Golgi-derived membranous organelles (MOs) in structures called Fibrous Bodies (FBs). These MSP-laden FB-MO complexes facilitate the subsequent segregation of MSP to budding spermatids and away from central residual bodies. Here we identify SPE-55 as a key FB assembly factor. In spe-55 spermatocytes, MSP remains diffusely cytosolic, and minimal MSP segregates to spermatids. The resulting spe-55 spermatozoa are motility-defective. SPE-55 localizes directly to MOs where it recruits the intrinsically disordered protein SPE-18 to initiate FB assembly, yet unlike SPE-6 or SPE-18, SPE-55 is required neither to complete meiosis nor to produce spermatids. Our study reveals an essential interplay between localized kinases and intrinsically disordered proteins in assembling large cytoskeletal complexes.

papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have attracted much attention for healthcare applications, demonstrating strong potential in automating conversational interactions. However, cloud-hosted systems raise privacy concerns and text-based interfaces can be difficult for children, older adults, and individuals with language impairments. Edge-deployed, voice-enabled LLM systems may address these barriers by keeping data local and using automatic speech recognition (ASR) for speech input. However, ASR transcripts often contain disfluencies, fillers, grammatical errors, and recognition noise, which may reduce downstream LLM performance for speakers with atypical language patterns. Here, we systematically evaluate edge-oriented ASR-LLM pipelines for individuals with language impairments using comparison studies and ablation experiments across aphasia, child language impairment, and dementia datasets. We identify transcript errors, repetition, noise, and input length as factors affecting system performance and deployment feasibility. These findings highlight key challenges for building more reliable and accessible speech-enabled AI systems for healthcare applications.
